name: Bull Flag

card.context: A leader with RS 80 or more, above the 200-day and a rising 50-day, has just made a fast pole: 20% or more in 20 sessions or fewer, often on a catalyst. The first flag after a base breakout or a market correction is the best one. Green or Yellow market.
card.pattern: A short rest of 3 to 15 sessions that drifts sideways or down, gives back at most half the pole and at most 15% from the pole top, on volume below the pole's, with every close holding the rising 21-day EMA.
card.trigger: PREV DAY HIGH BREAK: a session trades above the prior day's high inside or at the top of the flag, bought at market, no more than 4% past it. A support reclaim inside the flag and the flag-top break are the other two triggers.
card.stop: A few cents under the entry day's low or the prior day's low, usually within about 3% of the buy. The flag low is where the idea dies, not the stop.
card.failure_mode: The break stalls and price rolls back through the entry day's low within days, or the flag deepens, turns loose and closes under the 21-day EMA without reclaiming it. Seven in ten fixed-stop entries come back to the stop before 3R; the small stop and the next trigger are the answer.

criteria.statement: The close is above the 200-day simple moving average on every flag session and at the entry.

measure.what: close against the 200-day SMA

criteria.evidence: 98.5% of the app's flag fires were already above the 200-day (4.6). The app's own guard only blocks a falling 200-day; the house rule blocks any long under it.

criteria.dossier_basis: my proposal, from the app's judged textbook check (5.2)
criteria.evidence: The 10-session window is the textbook check's; the glossary's rising_average uses the same window for the 50-day.

criteria.statement: RS rating 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.

measure.what: RS rating

criteria.evidence: Kullamagi scans the top 1% to 2% movers; Bonde ranks 65-day momentum; Bracco wants the first flag in the hottest theme. Not coded in the scan; every one of the ten examples was at or near a 6-month high at the pole top.

criteria.statement: Price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day on the 50-day average.

measure.what: close

a_plus: bf.pole_strong: 30% or more, fast, on a catalyst, an HVE or an earnings gap, heavy volume
bf.which_flag: the first flag after a base breakout or a market correction
bf.depth_shallow: a third of the pole or less, 10% or less (the scan says deeper did slightly better)
bf.rides_fast_averages: rides the 9/10-day, short and shallow
bf.volume_dry: dries to the flag's lowest in the last 2 to 3 days
bf.inside_day_before: an inside day or narrow-range day before the trigger
bf.breakout_volume: 1.5x average or more, closing near the high
bf.earnings_flag: a post-earnings pole, or a flag above a flat base (Bulkowski)
bf.leadership: RS 90 or more, the leading theme, a Green market
b_minus: bf.which_flag: the third or later flag
bf.depth_half_pole: near half the pole, ragged
bf.holds_21ema: one close under the 21-day EMA, reclaimed the next day
no_trade: bf.inv_depth: over half the pole or 15% from the top
bf.inv_ema: closes under the 21-day EMA and stays
bf.inv_heavy_red: heavy red days in the flag
bf.stop_width: wider than the ADR or 5%
bf.no_chase: more than 4% past the trigger
bf.liquidity: under $10 or under $20 million a day
bf.market_reading: Red, or Orange unless A+

lookalikes.tell: Measure the pole. A bull flag follows a 20% to 30% run in 20 sessions or fewer; a high tight flag follows a near-double, 90% or more in 40 sessions or fewer, and rests 5 to 30 sessions.
Count the sessions since the pole top. A flag is done in 3 to 15 sessions and is a base past 20; a flat base rests at least 25 sessions in a box up to 15% deep with a flat ceiling tapped twice.
Look for shrinking pullbacks. A flag is one short drift on lighter volume; a VCP strings two to six pullbacks over 15 sessions or more, each smaller than the last, before its pivot.
Find the pole. A flag needs a 20% run in the 20 sessions before the rest; a pullback to the 10, 20 or 50-day with no pole is a moving-average pullback, setup 12.
Count again. Kullamagi's breakout rests 2 weeks to 2 months (10 to 40 sessions) after a 30% move; a flag rests 3 to 15 sessions. Past 20 sessions the card sends it to the base lessons.

invalidations: Before entry: more than 20 sessions since the pole top (bf.inv_length).
Before entry: a close under the 21-day EMA not reclaimed the next session (bf.inv_ema).
Before entry: the depth passes half the pole or 15% from the top (bf.inv_depth).
Before entry: two or more heavy red days on 1.5x volume (bf.inv_heavy_red).
Before entry: the pause wedges up (bf.inv_wedge_up).
Before entry: the third flag in a short run without a base (bf.inv_third_flag).
Before entry: a report within 3 sessions, wait (bf.earnings_window).
Before entry: the market reads Red, or Orange unless A+ (bf.market_reading).
After the entry: the stop is the exit, with the time stop (bf.after_entry_stop, bf.time_stop).
After the entry: a close under the flag's low means the idea is dead (bf.inv_close_under_flag_low).
mistakes: Buying the pole or chasing far above the trigger. The owner: OUST here would be a total chase.
Calling a deep, loose, jagged pullback a flag. Bulkowski: a loose flag meanders and looks jagged.
Ignoring volume: a flag on heavy, irregular volume is distribution, not a rest.
Using the flag low as the stop when it is 8% to 15% away, then sizing too big or skipping the stop-width check.
Waiting for a confirmation breakout and getting stopped in the chop below it (the owner's JOBY).
Buying the third or fourth flag late in a run (the owner's FCEL; Edwards and Magee's two surges).
Mistaking a wedge up for a flag.
Sitting in a forever flag with no trigger (the owner's AMZN note; the time stop).
Adding to a flag trade or averaging down.
Expecting the shape alone to pay. Measured, it does not: whatever edge there is comes from the leader, the catalyst, the market and the management.
Reading Brooks's bull flag (any pullback in a bull trend) as this setup. Ours needs a pole.

short_mirror.note: The bear flag, mirrored line by line (dossier 8.6): below the 200-day only, a falling 50-day, RS 20 or less in the weakest groups, not hard to borrow; a sharp drop of at least 20% within 20 sessions, then a 3 to 15-session drift up on lighter volume that retraces at most half the drop and stays under the falling 21-day EMA; short at market on a break of the prior day's low or the flag's low; stop a few cents above the day's high or the prior day's high; trims and trail mirrored. No dossier of its own. UCT has used the idea (a low grind bear flag; ChartMaster's RDDT). The app's bear_flag detector is hidden as noise. Bulkowski's down breakouts fail 45% of the time with an 8% average decline. Whether to teach it now is D-001.

best_conditions: A Green market, with the indexes above a rising 20-day EMA (the dossier's proposal, not a rule), and best of all the first flags in the leading theme after a breakout or a market correction. The first flags after a correction are usually a bit uncomfortable and wheezy. Edwards and Magee's warning stands: flags cluster late in a bull market.

management.trail: a close under the 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one (E52); his own flags lean to the 20 EMA
management.breakeven: between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default (B19)
management.gap_open: a trim level the day opens past is taken at the open (F63)
management.gap_against: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if past 2R (B20)
management.climax: sell a big part into a climax run (C34)
management.overrides: none. The dossier (8.4) finds nothing setup-specific is needed. Not ours: the app's 2R and 3R targets, the classical detector's full-pole target and its scale out at 1R, Kullamagi's sell a third to a half after 3 to 5 days. The measured move is a reference only (D-013).

base_rate.window: 60 sessions forward, fixed stop at the entry-day low, no trims, no breakeven, no trail, no time stop; 1996-02 to 2026-11; the T2 trigger (prior day's high) on flags of 3 to 15 sessions; one hit per flag

failures.why: a textbook-looking five-day flag (pole +62% in 14 days on an April 2019 gap, flag 8.9% deep on 0.44x the pole's volume, stop 1.8%); the trigger day was the high and the stock fell about 25% in four weeks. The pole was a one-day gap, not a trend, and the flag sat in the pole's third week.

a four-day flag 3.1% deep on a quarter of the pole's volume; it broke out, failed within days (best 0.85R), hit the 1.8% stop, then ran to 50 without us. A clean shape still loses about seven times in ten before 3R under a fixed stop; the answer is the small stop and the next trigger, not a wider stop.

a five-day flag at all-time highs after a +30% pole, stop 2.25%, best 0.56R; the breakout failed the same week and the stock drifted under the 50-day for two months. A later flag in a long run, in a stock already extended on the weekly chart.

A 5-day flag 6.7% deep (26% of a 36% pole) on 0.71x the pole's volume. The trigger day traded through the prior high and closed at the low of its range (271.99) on 0.69x volume; the stop was 1.78% under the fill against a 3.91% average daily range and the next session's low (270.60) took it.

examples.limits: No RS rating, group rank, market colour or flag count in the scan; the intraday T1 reclaim cannot be seen on daily bars; survivorship (the database leans to names that still trade); a fixed stop. Nothing here is a published statistic. Bulkowski's own flag counts are weak: 44% break-even failures, Not ranked.

near_misses.why: pole +18.2% in 20 sessions; the rule is 20% or more. A tidy 5-day, 4.7% pause on 0.75x volume, but the rise before it was 18.2% in 20 sessions. No pole, no flag: a pullback in an uptrend, judged under the moving-average pullback card (setup 12). Best 1.58R, stopped.

flag of 21 sessions; the rule is 3 to 15 (16 to 20 B-), past 20 it is a base. A 30% pole and a 6.6%-deep pause on 0.81x volume that ran 21 sessions. Past 20 sessions it is a base, judged as a flat base (setup 01) or a Qullamaggie consolidation (setup 18). Best 0.0R, stopped.

flag low gives back 55% of the pole; the rule is half or less. A 7-day flag only 12.8% under the top on half the pole's volume, but the low gave back 55% of the pole. A pullback that retraced more than half the pole is a deeper retest, closer to a pullback to the 21 EMA or the 50-day (setup 12) than to a flag. Best 3.01R, stopped.

flag highs rise +5.6% across the flag; the rule is a flat or falling line of highs. A 7-day pause 10.7% deep after a 58% pole, but its highs rose 5.6% across the pause. Higher highs and higher lows through the rest is a wedge up (bf.inv_wedge_up), not a flag. Best 0.0R, stopped.

conflicts: Sources: this dossier's section 11 is a table without ids, so every S-id on this card is the row's position in reading order, as the validator reads it (S1 Edwards and Magee, S2 Murphy, S3 ChartSchool, S4 Bulkowski's flags page, S6 his earnings flag, S8 Kullamagi, S10 to S13 Bonde, S15 Zanger, S20 the UCT Substack, S21 the rulebook, S22 the owner's verdicts, S24 the scanners, S25 the app pages, S26 the study notes). The dossier's own basis tags are kept in dossier_basis where a line's basis is a translation of them.

Length, five answers: Bulkowski under 3 weeks; Murphy 1 to 3 weeks; Edwards and Magee 5 days to 3 weeks, 4 weeks at most; ChartSchool up to 12 weeks (ideally 1 to 4); Kullamagi 2 weeks to 2 months. The owner's own examples run 2 to 4 days to about 2 weeks. The card takes 3 to 15 sessions, 16 to 20 as B-, past 20 a base (D-045).

The pole: no classic source gives a number; Kullamagi 30% to 100%+; the app's detectors 8% (bull_flag), 20% (the textbook check) and 40% (uct_flag_htf). The card takes 20% in 20 sessions with 30% as the A+ cue (D-029).

Depth: Edwards and Magee's 40% to 50% correction is their deepest buy point, not a maximum; the Model Book playbook's one third to one half is not the owner's words; uct_flag_htf allows 62%; the textbook check 12% and half the pole. The card takes half the pole and 15% from the top (D-046). The scan found 10% to 15% deep slightly better than 10% or less, which cuts against the A+ cue bf.depth_shallow.

Slope: the classics want a drift against the trend; Kullamagi allows flat channels and triangles; Edwards and Magee allow a rare flag that slopes up a trifle. The card accepts flat or down and rejects up-sloping, stricter than Edwards and Magee.

Volume in the flag: a requirement (Edwards and Magee, Murphy) against a tendency (Zanger, Bonde, ChartSchool), a frequency (Bulkowski's 74%) and silence (Kullamagi); uct_flag_htf has no volume test at all. The card makes it a gate pending D-006. Rule 8 forbids one heavy red day while 8.5 invalidates on two; the card keeps both (one drops the grade, two end the flag).

The trigger: a trendline pierce (Murphy, Bulkowski) against the pattern's high (Bulkowski's earnings flag), the opening-range high (Kullamagi), buying inside the flag (Edwards and Magee, the owner) and buying the open in anticipation (Bonde). The card leads with the owner's support reclaim and prior-day-high break and allows the flag-top break (D-027).

The stop: the flag low (both app detectors, the Model Book playbook) is a median 9.7% away; the house stop is the day's low or the prior day's low within about 3% (A3, A13). The house wins; the flag low is the invalidation. Whether flags get a hard 5% or ADR cap is D-005.

Targets: Edwards and Magee and Murphy add the pole at the breakout; Bulkowski 46% of the swing from the flag bottom; the app's detectors 2R and 3R or the full pole; Kullamagi has none and sells a third to a half after 3 to 5 days. The house trims win; the measured move is a reference only (D-013).

Reliability: Edwards and Magee, Murphy, Zanger and the Model Book playbook call flags among the most reliable patterns with no count; Bulkowski's counts are weak (44% break-even failures, Not ranked) and the app's Flag tag is withheld after a negative outcome replay. The dossier's own scan found no crude edge in the shape; the examples and the base rate lean on selection and management.
The 21-day EMA: the textbook check allows no close under it; the owner buys undercuts that close back above. The card allows one close reclaimed the next session (D-047).
The 200-day and liquidity: uct_flag_htf only blocks a falling 200-day and uses a $2 and $10,000 floor; B26 and B23 win.

Names: the Model Book card Bull Flag, the journal tag Classic Flag/Pullback, the setup tag Flag, the classical bull_flag detector and the Pattern Vision rubric are five names for one idea, not aliased; the vocabulary file says Bull Flag and Classic Flag/Pullback are the same setup; pullbacks to an average with no pole go to setup 12 (D-002). Flags with a 90%+ pole go to setup 03 (D-002).

The classical bull_flag narrative makes claims with no source: Raschke's Holy Grail as the same setup, Kullamagi hunting daily flags inside weekly breakouts, Schabacker 1932, a non-negotiable 1.5x volume rule, scaling out at 1R. None is used on this card (D-010). The Model Book playbook text is not the owner's words (D-014 is not in this dossier's register rows; question 14 maps to D-010).
Brooks's bull flag is any minor pullback in a bull trend with no pole; taught only so members are not confused by the term.
The short mirror (8.6) has UCT usage but no source that teaches it as a short; the app's bear_flag detector is hidden as noise. D-001.
